numerical_and_memory_risks: No GPU forward/backward was performed for this new method. Hidden-state return with nonreentrant checkpointing, CUDA numerical finiteness, runtime and peak allocation still require actual bounded execution and cannot be inferred from this source review.

Working current and replay graphs coexist until one micro backward;25 full-sequence hidden states, detached max targets and FP32 MSE conversions, plus frozen slow hidden outputs and target-head logits materially increase peak training allocation beyond plain r8. Frozen EMA itself is only2162688bytes and is not a bound on total overhead. No promise of fitting or faster training is made.

All masks still compute full working/slow/target-head diagnostics to match arithmetic; gate=0 does not eliminate teacher/hidden computation. Report actual training memory/time and do not market the rule as zero-cost.

Same training/dropout policy does not mean working and slow share an identical dropout realization. The NLL gate is a noisy same-forward proxy and cannot certify old knowledge, all-layer target quality, gradient improvement or F1.

Shuffle preserves per-update acceptance counts; size1 or all0/all1 reference vectors may have no sample-assignment change. Actual applied-vs-reference Hamming/degenerate counts must be reported from sealed scalar ledgers before interpreting a quality difference.

Naive baseline trained GPU0 while these three arms train GPU2. Mechanism comparison is among the three same-card arms; naive differences also contain ER/EMA exposure and hardware identity. Shared GPU1 final resource windows remain the comparable inference measurement.
